# pbs_node_certificate_renew (Action)

Renews the ACME certificate of a Proxmox Backup Server node now: PBS orders a new certificate from the CA of the node's ACME account, for the node's ACME domains — both set with `pbs_node_acme` —, installs it and has its proxy load it, without restarting; connections open before keep the old one. It is what `proxmox-backup-manager acme cert order` does on the host.

**PBS renews on its own.** Its daily update renews the certificate once it is due, on a node with ACME domains, so this action is for renewing earlier: with `force`, after changing the node's ACME account, domains or DNS plugin, or to see that renewal works. Without `force`, PBS renews only a certificate that is due — one that expires within a third of its lifetime from PBS 4.1.9 (half of it, for a certificate that lives less than ten days, from 4.1.10; three days at least), within 30 days before 4.1.9 — and the action otherwise succeeds without renewing, saying when the certificate expires. The self-signed certificate PBS generates is never due; a forced renewal replaces it with an ACME certificate, as `pbs_node_certificate` does when it orders one.

Before PBS is asked, the action checks that the node has ACME domains and that its ACME account exists: PBS would renew nothing without domains, and fail without the account. A renewal that fails sends PBS's ACME error notification, as a failed renewal of the daily update does. While it waits, the action reports the lines the task logs; a failure names the cause the task reports, and ends with the end of the task's log. PBS writes a renewed certificate even when its proxy cannot load it, and ends the task well: the action fails when the proxy still serves the certificate it served before the renewal, and warns when that was not the one PBS reported then, as `pbs_node_certificate` explains.

**The fingerprint changes** with the new certificate. While it renews, the provider keeps a connection open that it trusted before, reads the new certificate over it, and trusts it for the rest of the run, whatever the provider's TLS settings; it warns when they need changing before the next run — a pinned `tls_cert_fingerprint` (or `PBS_TLS_FINGERPRINT`) above all. Whatever else pins the old fingerprint fails too: Proxmox VE's PBS storage (`fingerprint` of `proxmox_storage_pbs`), other PBS syncing from this one. Trust a certificate of a public CA by the CA instead, as `pbs_node_certificate` explains.

**With `pbs_node_certificate`.** With `source = "acme"`, its next refresh reads the renewed certificate into its computed attributes, without planning anything, as after a renewal of the daily update. A change of its `triggers` orders a certificate already: do not trigger a forced renewal from the same change — new domains, when `triggers` follow them as in its example —, or PBS orders two certificates, which both count against the CA's rate limits. Neither PBS nor the provider can tell an uploaded certificate from an ordered one — one of a private CA for the node's domains looks the same —, and PBS renews whatever certificate the node serves, in its daily update too; so does the action:

~> On a node with ACME domains that serves a custom certificate — `source = "custom"` — a forced renewal replaces it with an ACME one, and the next apply of `pbs_node_certificate` uploads the custom certificate again. Remove the node's ACME domains to keep a custom certificate, as `pbs_node_certificate` warns.

Needs `Sys.Modify on /system/certificates`, and `Sys.Audit on /system` to check the node's ACME settings.

-> Actions need Terraform 1.14.1 or later. OpenTofu and older Terraform releases do not support them, and Terraform 1.13 ignores `action` blocks without a word; set `required_version = ">= 1.14.1"` in configurations that use them. An action runs when a resource's `lifecycle` `action_trigger` fires, or with `terraform apply -invoke=action.<type>.<name>`, which also refreshes the state of the resources the action's configuration refers to, and of those they depend on, but of no other resource.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  # Actions need Terraform 1.14.1 or later; Terraform 1.13 would ignore them.
  required_version = ">= 1.14.1"
}

# ACME settings as in the pbs_node_acme example, with its account and
# plugin. When they change — another account, say, of Let's Encrypt's
# production directory rather than its staging one — renew the certificate
# at once, rather than when PBS's daily update finds it due. Or invoke the
# action yourself, to see that renewal works:
# terraform apply -invoke=action.pbs_node_certificate_renew.now
#
# Do not trigger it so on a node with a pbs_node_certificate whose triggers
# follow the domains, as in its example: a change of domains has that
# resource order a certificate already, and the action would order a second
# one, which counts against the CA's rate limits too.
resource "pbs_node_acme" "this" {
  account = pbs_acme_account.letsencrypt.name

  domains = [
    { domain = "pbs.example.net", plugin = pbs_acme_plugin.cloudflare.id },
  ]

  lifecycle {
    action_trigger {
      events  = [after_update]
      actions = [action.pbs_node_certificate_renew.now]
    }
  }
}

action "pbs_node_certificate_renew" "now" {
  config {
    # Renew even though the certificate is not due yet.
    force   = true
    timeout = "15m"
  }
}
```

<!-- action schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `force` (Boolean) Whether to renew the certificate even when it is not due yet. Defaults to `false`: PBS then renews only a certificate that is due, and the action otherwise succeeds without renewing. Mind the CA's rate limits.
- `node` (String) Node whose certificate to renew: `localhost`, which every PBS answers to, or the node's host name. Defaults to the provider's `node`.
- `timeout` (String) How long to wait for the renewal, as a Go duration such as `10m`. Defaults to the provider's `task_timeout`. The action always waits: the provider has to read the new certificate before it can trust it. When the time runs out, the action fails, and the PBS task goes on — PBS cannot stop an ACME order — and installs the certificate if the CA issues it.
